message.text:
q15.

user: **`User` (`store.User`) — `store/user.go`** (line 29)
attachment: **`Attachment` (`store.Attachment`) — `store/attachment.go`** (line 16)
reaction: **`Reaction` (`store.Reaction`) — `store/reaction.go`** (line 7)

Each mirrors its table's columns: `User` carries `Username`, `Role`, `Email`, `Nickname`, `PasswordHash`, `AvatarURL`, and `Description` alongside the standard `RowStatus`/`CreatedTs`/`UpdatedTs`; `Attachment` carries `Filename`, `Blob`, `Type`, `Size`, `StorageType`, `Reference`, `Payload`, and the related memo ID; and `Reaction` is the smallest, with `ContentID` plus `ReactionType`:

```7:14:/bench/repo/store/reaction.go
type Reaction struct {
	ID        int32
	CreatedTs int64
	CreatorID int32
	// ContentID is the id of the content that the reaction is for.
	ContentID    string
	ReactionType string
}
```

The corresponding SQL is in `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` and its Postgres and MySQL counterparts, with the per-dialect query code in `store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}/user.go`, `attachment.go`, and `reaction.go`. Note that each of these files also defines sibling `Find*`/`Update*`/`Delete*` parameter structs, which are query descriptors rather than row mappings.
